answer: Lotus-Meadow Quill Shuffle: each epoch, agents commit ballots to a public beacon whose seed is revealed only after commit via verifiable delay function. The protocol shuffles agents into small signing quads; only quads whose aggregate ballot matches the revealed seed earn routing rights. Attackers cannot precompute favorable seeds, so sybils must control entire quads per epoch, multiplying identity cost by quad size and forcing continuous beacon-seeded registration spend that yields no persistent advantage.
